summary: A principled statistical-physics analysis of why softmax attention outperforms linear/kernelized alternatives, using a stylized single-location regression task with variable sequence length. The central results are clean and interpretable: softmax attention achieves the Bayes risk in population (satisfying a Nishimori condition) while linear attention provably falls short, and softmax retains its advantage in the finite-sample regime characterized via the replica method. The work is well-motivated and honestly scoped, but the model is highly idealized (single layer, no learnable query, Gaussian data) and the finite-sample characterization is non-rigorous, so significance rests on the elegance of the toy analysis rather than direct impact on practice.
strengths: Well-motivated question grounded in a real empirical puzzle (softmax's retrieval advantage from Shen et al.), turned into a tractable, analyzable task (spiked-SLR and max-SLR unified under a reweighted-Gaussian data model).

Clean, interpretable separation results: Prop. 4.2 shows softmax reaches Bayes risk exactly under a condition satisfied by both task variants, while Cor. 4.3–4.4 give explicit gaps for linear attention, tying the deficiency to poor normalization under variable sequence length.
Careful decomposition of which activation properties matter (exponential growth + all-token normalization) via comparison of linear, element-wise erf, and softplus-kernel attention.

Substantial technical contribution in the finite-sample replica characterization (Result 5.1), with numerical evidence that a quasi-Newton ERM matches the prediction, and honest acknowledgement that the derivation is non-rigorous.
Strong calibration: limitations (no query vectors, single layer, replica non-rigor, softmax not Bayes-optimal at finite α) are stated plainly rather than buried.

key_concerns.issue: Generality is narrow relative to the framing 'Statistical Advantage of Softmax Attention.' All results concern a single-location, single-layer, query-free predictor on Gaussian data; the leap from this to the observed advantage of softmax in real LLM retrieval is asserted by analogy (via Fig. 1 borrowed from prior work), not demonstrated.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Temper the title/abstract to reflect the toy setting, and/or add at least a small experiment on a more realistic proxy (e.g., MQAR-style associative recall with learned queries and >1 layer) to show the qualitative separation persists.

key_concerns.issue: The finite-sample core (Result 5.1) relies on the non-rigorous replica method plus a replica-symmetry/diagonal-order-parameter (manifold) assumption whose validity is only numerically checked; the manifold restriction is acknowledged to exclude other local minima, so the claimed 'computational advantage' is not fully established.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide either a rigorous argument (even for a special case) or systematic numerical stress-tests of replica symmetry / manifold stability across α, ν, L, and random seeds, and soften 'computational advantage' claims accordingly.

key_concerns.issue: Numerical results (Figs. 2–3) report no seeds, error bars, or variance for the simulated ERM markers, so the excellent theory–simulation agreement cannot be assessed for robustness.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report multiple seeds with error bars for the ERM markers and quantify the deviation between simulation and the replica prediction.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is partly incremental over an already-developed sequence multi-index / Bayes-optimal framework (Cui 2025; Troiani et al. 2025; Marion/Author et al. 2025), and several concurrent works (Dohmatob 2025; Barnfield et al. 2026; Dragutinović et al. 2025) address closely related questions; the specific delta needs sharper delineation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a short paragraph or table explicitly contrasting the new results (variable-length normalization, softmax = Bayes, finite-α separation) against each concurrent/prior work.

questions_for_authors: How sensitive are the separation results to the Gaussianity of tokens and to the specific weight functions g_ν? Do the qualitative conclusions survive heavier-tailed or correlated token distributions?
Does the softmax = Bayes result depend critically on the absence of a learnable query vector, or would it extend to a standard attention layer with learned Q?

For Result 5.1, what is the empirical evidence (across seeds and parameter ranges) that replica symmetry and the manifold assumption hold, and how does the quasi-Newton ERM behave when initialized adversarially off the manifold?
Can any part of the finite-sample characterization be made rigorous, and how large is the gap between the replica prediction and finite-N,D simulations as a function of dimension?
calibration_check: Claims are largely well-scoped to the toy setting with explicit limitations, though the title's broad 'Statistical Advantage of Softmax Attention' slightly overreaches relative to a single-location, single-layer, query-free analysis.

significance.justification: Offers a clean, principled explanation for softmax's retrieval advantage that the theory community would cite, but the toy setting limits direct impact on LLM practice.

novelty.justification: The variable-length normalization analysis and the softmax-reaches-Bayes result are new, but build incrementally on an existing multi-index/replica framework alongside several concurrent works.

rigor.justification: Population-level propositions appear rigorous, but the key finite-sample result uses the non-rigorous replica method plus an unproven manifold/replica-symmetry assumption.

statistical_soundness.justification: Simulations match theory well, but no seeds, error bars, or variance are reported for the ERM experiments, leaving robustness unquantified.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations (no query, single layer, non-rigor, softmax not finite-sample Bayes-optimal) are stated openly rather than hidden, though the title is mildly overbroad.

clarity.justification: Logical organization and clearly stated propositions, but very notation-heavy and dense, making the finite-sample section hard to follow without the appendices.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (intro, related work, model, population analysis, finite-sample analysis) applied well and within reasonable length.

reproducibility.justification: Theoretical results are reproducible from the stated propositions and code is mentioned, though key derivations and experimental settings live in unseen appendices.

related_work.justification: Thorough, fair positioning against kernelized attention, SSMs, multi-index models, and concurrent works, with a clear statement of the intended delta.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative comparisons (population risk across activations in Fig. 2; finite-α test risk vs. Bayes-optimal in Fig. 3) that directly support the claims, though lacking variance annotations.

breadth_generality.justification: Evidence spans two task variants and a few activations but a single toy architecture and data distribution, under-supporting the broadly framed advantage claim.

overall_recommendation.justification: A sound, elegant, and honestly scoped theory contribution sitting at the borderline-accept bar, limited mainly by the idealized setting and non-rigorous finite-sample analysis.
